title: The Telegram admin category menus and the /unsubscribe redirect pair
why: Five keyboard categories fan out to eighteen distinct `admin_run_*` actions behind nineteen buttons — `admin_run_cashiers` is deliberately listed twice, in Аналитика and in Команда. The categories are folders, not capabilities: every callback already maps one-to-one onto an existing `cmd_*` command in the dispatcher's action map, so each becomes a capability the owner asks for in words and the category level disappears entirely. The sixth row is not an admin menu at all: `/unsubscribe` and `/subscribe` now print one identical app-link redirect (bot.py L576-589), so marketing revocation no longer exists in this channel. Folding the folders away is navigation work; the revocation promise still printed on the opt-in screen is the part that has to be fixed.
disappear: The five category keyboards, the ← Назад chain back to the main panel, and the two redirect-only command bodies. The admin gate does not disappear: `canonical_staff_access.is_admin()` runs server-side in the bot process, and the five categories share one check in the dispatcher (bot.py L1298) rather than carrying one each. Removing the keyboards is therefore authority-neutral — the check sits in the handler, not in the button, so this neither loosens nor tightens who can run what. What does quietly disappear is the read-only grouping of Аналитика, today the only place in the whole console where the safe-versus-destructive distinction is expressed at all; a flat merge erases it.
remain: Every `admin_run_*` capability that works today, gated server-side exactly as it is now. Four of the seven job buttons do not work today — `react`, `cycle` and `sub_now` answer with `retention_owner_required`, `reviews` answers with an app link — so parity here means carrying forward four refusals, not four runnable jobs. The reassurance copy on the jobs screen («Все эти рассылки и так запускаются автоматически по расписанию») must travel into the capability description; it has no other home, and without it owners will believe manual runs are required. `admin_run_cashiers` must keep both entry points rather than being deduplicated away, and `admin_run_export` keeps its legally load-bearing read-only character. `admin_run_whatsnew` remains the owner's only preview of a client-facing card whose dismiss button is already retired (`whatsnew_dismiss`, legacy_client_entry.py L39).
risk: MEDIUM-HIGH — this group carries live defects, not only migration risk. Nothing in it is irreversible: the welcome-points backfill's own docstring states it is idempotent (bot.py L3740), so a repeat tap does not double-accrue, which is why this is not HIGH. But `admin_run_backfill` runs a one-time bulk accrual over YClients history on a single tap with no confirmation step, sitting in the same catch-all folder as the consent export — and it is not alone: `birthday`, `loy_now` and `ref_now` also fire immediately on one tap with no confirmation, and the birthday job sends promotional messages to real clients. Those three, plus the backfill and broadcast, must arrive behind the confirmation kind the contract assigns them, not behind a keyboard. The legal exposure is the larger one: the marketing opt-in screen (bot.py L445) still states consent can be revoked «командой /unsubscribe», and the client help text repeats the promise (L2670-2671, «отписаться от акций и промокодов»), while both commands now only print an app link. Neither is in the gate allow-list — `_GATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` at L353 holds only /start, /privacy and /cancel — so a gated client cannot reach even the redirect. Two screens promise a revocation route that no longer exists, and a fix aimed at only one of them leaves the other standing. Team management is thin in the same direction: staff binding is already retired, so after the merge this channel has no team surface at all and parity rests entirely on MAYA, which this sweep did not verify.
user_impact: Only the owner is affected, but not in the way stated: in the swept tree this console is already dead in the Telegram channel, so what the merge changes is a refusal becoming a capability, not a keyboard becoming words. `canonical_staff_access.current()` is populated only by the webhook server's aiohttp middleware (canonical_staff_access.py L156-198), and that module's own docstring states that native Telegram updates never acquire the context; bot.py never installs the middleware and never sets the ContextVar, so `is_admin()` is False for every Telegram update — `/admin` (L1281-1283) answers «Команда только для администраторов.» to the owner himself, and `_admin_dispatch` (L1298) refuses every `admin_cat_*`/`admin_run_*` tap. The folder walk (tap category → tap leaf → ← Назад) is what the code draws, not what the owner can reach; if the deployed VPS build predates the R02 cutover it may still hold there, so the entry must date the claim rather than assert it as today's behaviour. Parity is also overstated: the five keyboards carry 19 buttons / 18 distinct callbacks (`admin_run_cashiers` is cross-listed at L1232 and L1256), and at least six do not perform their action even with a valid principal — react/cycle/sub_now are `retention_owner_required` refusals (L1433-1442, L1070-1079, L1100-1109), reviews is a one-line app link (L3812-3813), ai_prov returns a `confirmation_link` URL (L1443-1450), and broadcast's send path `_broadcast_execute` (L3664-3668) returns `B35_CANONICAL_OWNER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED_USE_PANEL`. S-415's "low-risk, both already exist as commands" is wrong for a further reason: `_QueryAsUpdate` (L1266-1276) hands the category screen itself to the handler as `update.message`, so `cmd_broadcast` parses that screen's title «📣 Маркетинг и анонсы» as a text argument (L3573-3576) and the button skips the template menu entirely, opening a broadcast preview whose body is the menu label. Two pieces of context do vanish with the folders unless deliberately carried over — the line telling the owner these broadcasts already run on schedule (L1317-1319), and the Аналитика grouping together with its `# Аналитика (read-only)` comment (L1342), which is the only written record of which leaves only read. Clients are affected only by S-656, and the dead end is narrower than stated: while the opt-in screen is up the client is by definition still gated and `/unsubscribe` is not in `_GATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS` (L353), so the gate re-shows the consent screen and stops the update (L461-479); once they answer the marketing question, the same command reaches cmd_unsubscribe and returns an app-link redirect that revokes nothing in Telegram (L576-585). Either way the promise at L445 has no in-channel mechanism behind it, before the merge or after.
security_impact: NEUTRAL for authority, but not for the reason given. The gate is `canonical_staff_access.is_admin` at bot.py L1298, and it resolves through a request-scoped canonical principal that only the webhook server's aiohttp middleware ever establishes — so in this channel it is not a removable duplicate; it is the only check standing, and it already refuses everyone, the owner included. The premise that "every leaf re-checks it independently" is false: 15 of the 18 handlers call `is_admin` themselves (cmd_ai_cost L1387, cmd_export_consents L1408, cmd_loyalty_backfill L3743 among them), but cmd_whats_new (L551), cmd_reviews_now (L3812) and cmd_ai_provider (L1443) do not, and for those three the L1298 dispatch gate is the only admin check on the button path. No hole opens — none of the three mutates anything (a client-facing release card, an app link, and a URL the governed-settings endpoint must authorize server-side) — but the blanket claim would license deleting a router gate that is load-bearing for three leaves. The backfill defect as described does not exist: `loyalty.run_backfill_job` (loyalty.py L786-794) opens with `return _legacy_loyalty_mutation_disabled('backfill_legacy_loyalty')`, which raises `LegacyLoyaltyCutoverError`; the accrual body beneath it is dead code, and the same cutover disables admin_run_loy_now (`run_loyalty_job` L553-555) and admin_run_ref_now (referral resolver refusal, referral.py L211+). A tap on admin_run_backfill accrues nothing — it would surface to the owner as «Ошибка: p4_03_legacy_mutation_disabled:…» via the handler's except (L3767-3770). Calling that an existing gap, and its confirmation an improvement, inverts the facts and invites the one genuinely dangerous move available in this group: reading the conditional approval ("each `admin_run_*` carries its contract-assigned confirmation before the keyboard goes") as licence to re-wire a mutation that P4-03 and B35 deliberately fail-closed. Re-enabling it behind a confirm dialog would reverse a fail-closed decision while presenting itself as a safety improvement. If one leaf deserves the unconfirmed-bulk-effect flag it is `admin_run_birthday`, which is not cut over: `birthday.run_birthday_job` still writes promo rows and publishes real Telegram deliveries through `maya_inbox_bridge.publish_inbox_item`. Any confirmation added anywhere here remains role-gated — the same admin asks and confirms — and must never be described as separation of duties. The live consent defect stands as S-656 states it: the marketing opt-in at L445 still promises «Согласие можно отозвать в любой момент командой /unsubscribe» while both commands are redirect-only (L576-585) and neither is in the gate allow-list (L353); the comment block at L348-350 still documents them as gate exceptions that the allow-list no longer grants. Fixing the copy or restoring in-channel revocation is a genuine improvement; leaving both as-is leaves the defect exactly where it stands.
